evidence.ref: The intent corpus (schema warp.intent_corpus/v1, module .warp/intent_corpus.py) is built FROM the project's OWN recorded artifacts and reuses recorded data only (NG5, no new store, no new parser, no new instrumentation). build_corpus INDEXES the existing record through the repo's OWN readers, injected: validate.parse_yamlish for specs and plans, json for proofs and verdicts, validate.proof_digest for a proof's canonical identity, validate.plan_registry for the plans, validate.load_repo_contract for the architecture contract, and .warp/decision.py load_record for decision records (open_corpus loads validate.py and decision.py BY PATH, one parser, no import cycle). Over this repository it indexes 119 specs (with their acceptance criteria), 115 proofs (criteria statuses, checks, bound commit, proof digest), 117 verdicts, 15 plans, 459 events, and the architecture contract (contract_present true); decisions stand down (no .warp/decisions/ here). python3 .warp/intent_corpus.py prints those stats; python3 .warp/intent_corpus.py trace WARP-1202 returns the governance chain.

scripts/selftest.py WARP-1203 block: 'the corpus builds over this repository and indexes the real specs, proofs, and verdicts' (specs>0, proofs>0, verdicts>0, empty False). Fail-closed-at-build over a temp tree: 'a malformed spec (no front matter) fails closed at build time' (IntentCorpusError), 'a malformed proof manifest (invalid JSON) fails closed at build time' (IntentCorpusError). Adoption-safe: 'an empty corpus (no specs, no proofs) stands down' (empty True, trace/governing_spec ungoverned, no error).

The runtime query interface is a READ over the record (in-session, read-only). trace(spec_id) returns the governance chain: the acceptance criteria the spec PROMISED, the proof that PROVED it (per-criterion statuses, checks, bound commit, proof digest), the VERDICT that reviewed it, and citations listing the REAL artifact paths (spec file, proof manifest, verdict). governing_spec(behavior) resolves by recorded spec id or by declared footprint match (reporting candidates). proof_for_commit(commit) traces a change to the proof and verdict whose recorded commit it matches. recent_changes(path) reads BOTH git history (a synchronous in-session git log) AND the event stream (events whose recorded commit matches). area_of(module) resolves a module to its contract area. trace_incident(incident) assembles the artifact-grounded trace an incident resolves to (governing spec, criteria, proof, verdict, recent changes over the footprint, areas when a contract exists). This is the READ the responder loop WARP-1204 (W4) diagnoses FROM; this module composes no prose diagnosis and emits no proposal.

selftests: 'trace of a known spec cites its criteria, proof, and verdict, each a real artifact' (WARP-1202: criteria>=1, proof digest sha256:, proof criteria and checks present, verdicts>=1, citations resolve to proof/WARP-1202/manifest.json and verdict.json). 'governing_spec resolves a behavior by recorded spec id' (WARP-1202, matched_by spec_id) and 'by declared footprint match' (.warp/evidence.py resolves to WARP-1202, matched_by footprint, in candidates). 'proof_for_commit traces a change to the proof and verdict whose recorded commit it matches' (96fb65f -> WARP-1202, verdicts present). 'recent_changes reads BOTH git history and the event stream' (injected deterministic git reader: 2 git commits + >=1 joined event). 'trace_incident assembles the artifact-grounded trace for a seeded incident' (governing spec + proof + verdict + recent_changes).

Diagnosis from artifacts is ARTIFACT-GROUNDED, never fabricated (the load-bearing guarantee, C1). A behavior no recorded artifact governs returns a truthful Trace with governed false whose reason names 'no governing artifact' and which carries no invented spec, criterion, proof, or verdict; a spec with no recorded proof or verdict traces with proof None or verdicts empty (the absence is reported, never filled). The query surface fails closed by name on a malformed query: an empty or non-string spec id, path, behavior, or commit (via _require_query raising IntentCorpusError), and an incident naming neither an affected spec nor an affected behavior.

selftests: 'an ungoverned behavior returns a truthful Trace (no fabrication)' (governed False, 'no governing artifact' in reason, spec_id None, criteria [], proof None, verdicts []); 'the real corpus honors the no-fabrication guarantee'. THE NO-FABRICATION TOOTH: '_ICFabricator (a resolver mutated to FABRICATE a governor) turns the no-fabrication check RED' (governed becomes True for the ungoverned behavior). 'a spec with no recorded proof or verdict traces with the absence reported' (proof None) and THE PROOF-GROUNDING TOOTH: '_ICProofFabricator (a trace mutated to fabricate a dropped proof) turns the proof-grounding check RED' (proof becomes not None). Malformed-query refusals: trace(''), trace(None), governing_spec(''), recent_changes(None), proof_for_commit(''), area_of(None), and trace_incident of an incident with no affected_spec/affected_behavior each refuse.

Adoption safe and the cross-plan join is SOFT (C7), degrading down and never faking a join. With a PLAN-0011 architecture contract, area_of resolves a module to its declared areas and trace attaches the areas a spec's footprint and placement fall into (reusing arch.area_for_path). With NO contract, area_of returns {contract_present: false, areas: null} and trace attaches areas None, and trace_incident still resolves the governing spec, proof, verdict, and the recent changes (spec and git level) - so a party that never wrote the code still reaches a cited answer without a contract. The join is never faked: an absent contract yields None, never an invented area.

selftests: with a contract 'area_of resolves a module to its declared area' (.warp/validate.py -> contracts) and 'trace attaches the areas the spec's footprint and placement fall into' (WARP-1202 -> contracts). With NO contract (temp corpus, repo_contract (None,None)): 'area_of stands down honestly' (== {contract_present False, areas None}), 'trace stands down to spec and git level (areas None), never a faked area', and 'trace_incident degrades to spec and git level with no contract' (governing spec WARP-9002 + git changes over .warp/intent_corpus.py, areas None).

TEETH proven by mutation (anti-vacuity C1), each observed RED then reverted byte-identical (the load-bearing teeth are the AC3 no-fabrication and proof-grounding mutations and the AC4 C7 stand-down). IN-SESSION with no detached process: the only external program is a synchronous in-session git log over this repository's own history (subprocess.run over git, never Popen), subprocess imported LAZILY inside the git reader (not at module top), mirroring fleet.py's git worktree helper; a subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True) mutation turns the no-detach check RED. .warp/intent_corpus.py (594 lines, under the 1000 module_lines budget) and .warp/capabilities.yaml are byte-identical across root, plugin/templates, and all 6 packs (aider, antigravity, codex, copilot, cursor, opencode). capabilities.yaml gains ONE honest mechanical entry (intent_corpus, home .warp/intent_corpus.py) that defers honestly: the responder loop WARP-1204 (W4) is the first consumer, the evidence plane W2, whitelist W5, executor W6, and two-key W7 are referenced not built, and landing a corpus check into validate.py run_all and lay-down via init is WARP-1211 (W11). validate.py is NOT edited (stays 925 lines, under budget), matching how W1 and W2 shipped their organs unwired. No protected path is touched. RULE #1 clean (ASCII hyphen only; the '# ---' dividers are the established engine horizontal-rule convention, not a prose em-dash stand-in).
